input.summary:
Keeper aisle 2 furnished in parts/room-2.mjs: a dark oak keeper's desk with chair and standing lantern at the west end (focal), a hay-and-dresser store on the north wall, two hanging lanterns under the ceiling.
make.sh gives a whole build.nbt; room part reports 15 placed, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines. `mcd room` says OK: 16/16 floor cells reachable, min light 9, 0 dark cells.
The lane stays clear (door cell (15,3), row z 4 from x 15 to 20, nothing in front of the z 5 openings).
left: Not ticked in elements.md: the Light item covers all rooms and is the lamplighter's pass. This room is already lit (min 9), so it needs no extra lamps.
The room.png at this size is too small to judge the furniture detail; I checked the layout through the floor grid and light map, not by eye.
`mcd check` reports 8 orphan slabs and stairs outside this part (shopfront/roof rows); not from this room, left for those parts.
Only 15 blocks are placed: a sparse room, with no bed or table beyond the desk. The store is planks and hay with no trapdoor shelves.

waste.what: Worked out each furniture cell's x/z/y by hand and typed the layers() rows, then checked by reading the floor and light grids
waste.cost: about 6 layer rows and 3 legend entries, one draft; the room check passed on the first build
waste.tool: `mcd plan` could emit a blank layers() template with the walkable lane and the door/opening cells already marked, so only the furniture cells need typing

waste.what: Placed lantern positions by guessing, then read the light map to confirm they cleared the dark cells
waste.cost: one make.sh and room check cycle; no retries needed because min light was already 9
waste.tool: `mcd room --suggest` (or a lantern-spot step before drawing) so the lanterns are placed from the lit map before the furniture is drawn

waste.what: Read room.png to judge the layout, but at 440px the furniture was too small to read
waste.cost: one Read; the judgement had to rely on the text grids
waste.tool: `mcd rooms --zoom` or a per-room tile at 12px per block, so one look settles the furniture

companions.task: design the store along the north wall as trapdoor shelves and a proper dresser rather than planks with hay, and say which items sit where
confirm the two hanging lanterns and the desk lantern against the whole-building light pass, so the room's light matches the other rooms'
